info.title: Zenbu account service
info.description:
Accounts, sign-in, profiles, and sync for every Zenbu app (ADR 0013). Sign-in is Better Auth's, under /v1/auth; a test holds each of its answers to this contract.

- **Errors.** Every error is `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`. Branch on `code`, which is stable; `message` is for people and may change. A route may answer a code it doesn't list here, such as one from a Better Auth upgrade: handle it by its status.
- **Apps.** A sign-in names its app in `X-Zenbu-Client`, unless it comes from one of the website's origins; the app decides the scopes its tokens carry.
- **Bodies** are JSON, at most 64 KB (`413 too_large`), but a photo's upload, which is the photo's file.
- **Emails** are in the language a request names in `Content-Language`, `en` or `ja`, which needs no entry in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`. Without one, they are in the language the account was made with, or English. An account made with one keeps it, through Google's web sign-in too.
- **Rate limits** answer `429 too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`, in seconds (Better Auth's also with `X-Retry-After`).
- **Browsers** may call the service only from the website's origins, with credentials; CORS lets the page read `Retry-After` and `X-Retry-After`.

accessToken.description: A 15-minute access token from GET /v1/auth/token, which takes the session token a sign-in returns, never the session token itself. It names the account (`sub`), the app (`azp`), when the learner signed in (`auth_time`), and the app's scopes (`scope`, space-separated). Each route names the scope it needs, and each sync operation its own, in `x-sync-entities`. The dictionary service's routes for apps take `dictionary:read`.

sessionToken.description: The signed session token from a sign-in's `set-auth-token` header. Send it only to /v1/auth.

Error.description: Every error. `code` is stable and machine-readable; `message` is for people and may change.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters once trimmed, with runs of spaces made one, kept in Unicode NFC, and no control or invisible format characters.

username.description: 3 to 30 letters a to z, digits, or underscores after Unicode NFKC, trimming, and lowercasing, unique across accounts; `null` removes it.

headword.description: The word as the app shows it, kept in Unicode NFC and trimmed, with no control characters.

reading.description: Its reading, held as `headword` is. Empty when left out.

state.description: The state the word moves to.

headword.description: The word as the app shows it, kept in Unicode NFC and trimmed, with no control characters. Needed for `learning` and `known`; for `unknown` it is not read, and the word keeps the text it has.

reading.description: Its reading, held as `headword` is. For `learning` and `known`, empty when left out; for `unknown` it is not read, and the word keeps the reading it has.

stateChangedAt.description: When the word moved to the state, by the device's clock: ISO 8601, from 2000 on; a time after the service's is taken as the service's. Left out, it is the service's time when the change applies. A change that leaves the state as it was keeps the earlier time.

headword.description: The word as the app shows it, kept in Unicode NFC and trimmed, with no control characters.

reading.description: Its reading, held as `headword` is. Empty when left out.

stateChangedAt.description: When the word moved to the state, by the device's clock: ISO 8601, from 2000 on; a time after the service's is taken as the service's. Left out, it is the service's time when the change applies. A change that leaves the state as it was keeps the earlier time.

When the word moved to the state, by the device's clock: ISO 8601, from 2000 on; a time after the service's is taken as the service's. Left out, it is the service's time when the change applies. A change that leaves the state as it was keeps the earlier time.

name.description: 1 to 500 characters once trimmed; control characters become spaces.

position.description: Where the list sorts among the account's lists, lowest first.

name.description: 1 to 500 characters once trimmed; control characters become spaces.

position.description: Where the list sorts among the account's lists, lowest first.

watchedAt.description: ISO 8601, from 2000 on, by the device's clock; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

title.description: Cut to 200 characters; control characters become spaces, and an empty one is left out.

position.description: Where the learner was, in seconds.

comprehension.description: The share of the captions' words the learner knows.

text.description: The sentence as it was said: not blank, cut to 2,000 characters, with control characters made spaces.

translation.description: Its translation, cut to 4,000 characters, or null; null when left out.

language.description: The language it was said in.

bookmarkedAt.description: ISO 8601, from 2000 on, by the device's clock; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

item.description: A Language Reference ID (32 lowercase hex digits), `kanji:` and one kanji in Unicode NFC, or a note identity an earlier app saved (`wn1:` and 64 lowercase hex digits).

text.description: The note: 1 to 10,000 characters once trimmed, kept in Unicode NFC. Line breaks and tabs stay, and other control characters become spaces. Never cut: a longer note is refused.

headword.description: The headword the note was saved on, if any.

name.description: The photo's name, such as its file's. Cut to 200 characters, with control characters made spaces; it may be empty.

savedAt.description: ISO 8601, from 2000 on, by the device's clock; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

headword.description: The word as the app shows it, kept in Unicode NFC and trimmed, with no control characters.

reading.description: Its reading, held as `headword` is. Empty when left out.

savedAt.description: ISO 8601, from 2000 on, by the device's clock; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

photoId.description: The SHA-256 of the photo file, uploaded first with `PUT /v1/photos/{photoId}`.

value.description: The setting's value, of its kind: `x-sync-entities` lists each setting.

query.description: What was searched, as the app keeps it: 1 to 1,000 characters, with no control characters. Its HMAC-SHA256 in UTF-8, after Unicode NFC, keyed with the account's `searchKey`, is the `entityId`.

searchedAt.description: ISO 8601, from 2000 on, by the device's clock; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

id.description: The Zenbu user ID. It never changes.

email.description: The account's email. It can't be changed here.

version.description: The profile revision. It goes up by one with each change, and jumps to the time in milliseconds when the service starts on a restored backup; send it back as `baseVersion` to change the profile.

ProfileConflict.description: The profile changed since `baseVersion`. `current` is the profile as it is now.

baseVersion.description: The profile `version` this change was made to. If the profile has changed since, nothing is changed and the answer is a conflict with the current profile.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters once trimmed, with runs of spaces made one and no control characters. Stored in Unicode NFC.

username.description: 3 to 30 letters a to z, digits, or underscores, unique across accounts. It's normalized first (Unicode NFKC, trimmed, lowercased), so `Kana_Fan` is `kana_fan`. `null` removes it.

confirm.description: The learner confirmed in the app.

appleAuthorizationCode.description: From a fresh Sign in with Apple, for an account that signs in with Apple. It's used once, to revoke the app's access with Apple.

appleRedirectUri.description: The website only: the return URL its Sign in with Apple popup named, which Apple needs again to take the code. It must be on one of the website's origins. Without it, the website's code is taken as one Apple sent to GET /v1/auth/callback/apple.

changes.description: The entities that changed after the cursor, each once, as they are now, including the ones this request changed. On a page, lists and photos come before their words, but a word can come on an earlier page than its list or photo: hold it until the sync reaches `hasMore: false`.

cursor.description: Opaque, and at most 200 characters. Keep it once the changes are applied, and send it next time.

hasMore.description: More changes are waiting: sync again with the new cursor.

searchKey.description: To an app with `searches:read`: the account's key for recent searches' IDs, 64 hex digits. A recent search's `entityId` is the HMAC-SHA256 of its query, after Unicode NFC, under this key, so a removed search keeps nothing that reveals what was searched. Keep it with the account; it changes only if the service's secret does.

MutationResult.description: `applied`: the change is in, at `version`. `conflict`: the entity changed since `baseVersion`, so nothing changed; `current` is it as it is now. `rejected`: the change can never apply as sent; `error.code` says why. A result is final: to try again, send a new mutation with a new ID.

emptied.description: The photo was emptied, its last word removed, not deleted. Drop it and its words as for any delete, but no place among the account's files was freed: it keeps its file for 30 days, and a word added from elsewhere brings it back. Any other delete leaves this out.

Change.description: An entity as it is now (`put`, with `data`), or gone (`delete`): a deleted list, note, or photo, a word removed from a list or a photo, a video or search removed or past the newest the account keeps, a bookmark or the profile photo removed, a setting the account doesn't hold, or one never there. A `knownWord` at Unknown is still a `put`, with `state: "unknown"`.

state.description: The learner's state for the word. Always sent by this service; a service from before Learning, during a deploy or after a rollback, sends none, so read `known` instead.

known.description: Whether `state` is `known`, for an app that reads only this: a Learning word is not known.

stateChangedAt.description: When the word moved to its current state, as the app said, or the service's time when the change carried none; a time after the service's is taken as the service's. `null` for a word that moved to its state before the service kept the time; a service from before it sends none.

title.description: At most 200 characters: a longer one is cut, and control characters become spaces.

author.description: The channel, held as title is.

comprehension.description: The share of the captions' words the learner knows, 0 to 1.

watchedAt.description: When the learner last watched it, as the app said; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

text.description: The sentence as it was said, at most 2000 characters: a longer one is cut, and control characters become spaces.

translation.description: Its translation, at most 4000 characters, or null.

language.description: The language the sentence was said in.

bookmarkedAt.description: When the learner bookmarked it, as the app said; a time after the service's is taken as the service's.

itemId.description: The word, kanji, or note identity it is on.

id.description: The SHA-256 of its file: download it by this ID.

cursor.description: The `cursor` from the last answer whose changes the client applied. Leave it out, or send null, to start from the beginning.

limit.description: The most journal entries to read this time. Default 100.

mutations.description: Up to 50 changes made on the device, applied in order before the changes are read.

id.description: A client-made ID, unique for each mutation, such as a UUID. Sending the same mutation again under its ID never applies it twice, and gets the same outcome: applied at the same version, a conflict with the entity as it is then, or a rejection with the same `error.code`. Reusing an ID for a different mutation is rejected with `mutation_id_reused`.

entity.description: `profile`, `knownWord`, `list`, `listWord`, `watchedVideo`, `bookmarkedSentence`, `wordNote`, `photo`, `photoWord`, `profilePhoto`, `setting`, `recentSearch`. Any other is rejected with `unknown_entity`, and the rest of the request still applies. A change the app's scopes don't allow is rejected with `not_allowed`, and the app reads only the entities its scopes do.

operation.description: One of the entity's operations, in `x-sync-entities`, with the scopes each needs, the fields it takes, and whether it reads `baseVersion`. Any other is rejected with `unknown_operation`.

entityId.description:
- `profile`: The account's ID, or left out.
- `knownWord`: The item: a Language Reference ID (32 lowercase hex digits), or `kanji:` and one kanji, kept in Unicode NFC.
- `list`: Its UUID, in either case; answers name it in lowercase.
- `listWord`: The list's UUID, a slash, and the item: `<list>/<item>`.
- `watchedVideo`: The YouTube video ID: 11 letters, digits, `-`, or `_`.
- `bookmarkedSentence`: The sentence's UUID, in either case; answers name it in lowercase.
- `wordNote`: The note's UUID, in either case; answers name it in lowercase.
- `photo`: The SHA-256 of the photo's file, in 64 lowercase hex digits.
- `photoWord`: The photo's SHA-256, a slash, and the item: `<photo>/<item>`, the item as a note's is.
- `profilePhoto`: The account's ID, or left out.
- `setting`: The setting's name, from the list above.
- `recentSearch`: The HMAC-SHA256 of the query in UTF-8, after Unicode NFC, under the account's `searchKey` from the sync answer, in 64 lowercase hex digits: one query is one entity on every device, and a removed one keeps nothing that shows what was searched without the key. The examples use a key of 64 zeros.

baseVersion.description: The version of the entity the change was made to, or 0 for one the client has never seen. If the entity has changed since, what happens is the operation's rule, in `x-sync-entities`, which also says which operations read it.

fields.description: What the operation sets: the operation's fields, in `x-sync-entities`. Each value is a string, number, boolean, or null.

Mutation.description: One change made on the device. `x-sync-entities` holds each entity and its operations, and `x-sync-rejections` each code a rejected result can carry.

profile.description: The account's name and username. `PATCH /v1/me` changes them by the same rule; the email doesn't change here.
profile.entityId: The account's ID, or left out.

update.description: Name, username, or both. It applies only at the profile's current version, or conflicts with the profile as it is now; sending the current values again is applied and changes nothing.

knownWord.description: The learner's state for a word or a kanji: `unknown`, `learning`, or `known`, one at a time. An app that shows Learning changes it with `set`; `mark` and `clear` are for an app that sees only whether a word is known, and read a Learning word as not known. A word that goes back to Unknown stays, as a `put` with `state: "unknown"` and `known: false`.
knownWord.entityId: The item: a Language Reference ID (32 lowercase hex digits), or `kanji:` and one kanji, kept in Unicode NFC.

set.description: Moves the word to `state`, from any state to any other. It applies only if the word is still at `baseVersion` (0 for one the account never had), as `mark` and `clear` do, or conflicts with the word as it is now. Setting the state the word has is applied and changes nothing.

mark.description: Makes the word Known, from Unknown or Learning: the same change as `set` with `state: "known"`. It applies only if the word is still at `baseVersion` (0 for one the account never had), so a mark made before the learner cleared the word loses to the clear, and one made after seeing it wins. Marking a known word is applied and changes nothing.

clear.description: Makes a known word Unknown. It applies only at the word's current version: a clear that never saw a later mark conflicts, and the word stays known. Clearing a word not known, a Learning one too, is applied and changes nothing, since the app that sends it can't see Learning; `set` with `state: "unknown"` ends Learning.

list.description: A word list. An account holds at most 500, and a deleted list's ID can't be used again.
list.entityId: Its UUID, in either case; answers name it in lowercase.

create.description: Rejected `already_exists` if the account has or had a list with that ID, and `too_many_lists` past 500.

update.description: A rename, a move, or both. It applies only at the current version, so two renames conflict and the second gets the list as it is now; one that already matches the list is applied. An update of a deleted list conflicts with the `delete`.

delete.description: It always applies, wins over everything done to the list since, renames and words added elsewhere too, and takes the list's words with it: drop them on the device.

listWord.description: A word in a list. A list holds at most 5,000.
listWord.entityId: The list's UUID, a slash, and the item: `<list>/<item>`.

add.description: It always applies to a list the account has. To a deleted or unknown list it's rejected `unknown_list`, and past 5,000 words `list_full`. Adding a word the list has is applied and changes nothing.

remove.description: It applies only at the word's current version, so it removes only an add it saw: an add the remover never saw wins, and the remove conflicts. Removing a word the list hasn't is applied.

watchedVideo.description: A video the learner watched in the iOS app's Player. The account keeps the 50 most recently watched, and remembers the latest 100 videos it removed or pruned.
watchedVideo.entityId: The YouTube video ID: 11 letters, digits, `-`, or `_`.

watch.description: Send the whole video each time. A watch of a video the account has applies whatever its base version: the one with the later `watchedAt` sets the fields it sends, an older one sent late only fills fields the account lacks, and a field left out keeps the account's. A watch of a video the learner removed applies only at the removal's version, so one made before seeing the removal conflicts with the `delete`. A watch past the 50 newest prunes the oldest, which syncs as a `delete`.

remove.description: The learner removed the video. It always applies; removing one the account has not is applied and changes nothing.

bookmarkedSentence.description: A sentence the learner bookmarked in the iOS app's Translate tab, alone: never its conversation. An account holds at most 2,000.
bookmarkedSentence.entityId: The sentence's UUID, in either case; answers name it in lowercase.

add.description: It always applies; adding one the account has changes nothing, and past 2,000 it's rejected `too_many_bookmarks`.

remove.description: It applies only at the bookmark's current version, so it removes only an add it saw: an add the remover never saw wins, and the remove conflicts. Removing one the account hasn't is applied.

wordNote.description: A note the learner wrote on a word or a kanji, or one an earlier app saved under a note identity no word takes now. A word may have several. An account holds at most 10,000. A deleted note's row keeps only its ID and version.
wordNote.entityId: The note's UUID, in either case; answers name it in lowercase.

write.description: Writes the note whole: a new one at `baseVersion` 0, or a change to one at its current version. A write that matches the note is applied and changes nothing. A write at an older version conflicts with the note as it is now, so neither device's text is lost: keep yours as a new note on the same word, or, if `current`'s text is the one your change started from, write it again at `current`'s version. A write of a note deleted since `baseVersion` applies and brings it back: the deleter never saw that text. Past 10,000 notes it's rejected `too_many_notes`.

delete.description: It applies only at the note's current version, so it deletes only what the learner saw: a note written elsewhere since stays, and the delete conflicts. Deleting a note the account hasn't is applied.

photo.description: A photo in the learner's Media Library, by its file, which `PUT /v1/photos/{photoId}` uploads first and `GET /v1/photos/{photoId}` downloads. The account keeps the bytes as the app sent them. A photo is shown while it's on a word; removing its last word empties it, which syncs as a `delete` marked `emptied: true` but keeps its file for 30 days, and a word added from elsewhere brings it back. A photo left with no word for a day is emptied too. An emptied photo's file counts toward the account's 1,000 for its 30 days, so the word that brings it back always finds it; then it's deleted, which syncs as a plain `delete`, freeing its place.
photo.entityId: The SHA-256 of the photo's file, in 64 lowercase hex digits.

add.description: It always applies, once the account holds the file (else `photo_not_uploaded`): the same photo saved again after a delete or once emptied comes back. Adding one the account shows changes nothing. Send its words next, as `photoWord` adds.

delete.description: The learner deleted the photo. It always applies, wins over everything done to the photo since, words added elsewhere too, marks each of its words removed, and takes its file, unless the profile photo is the same file: drop them on the device. A word added later is rejected `unknown_photo`.

photoWord.description: A word or kanji a photo is on. A photo is on at most 500 words, and remembers its latest 500 removed ones; a deleted photo's words go when the account forgets the photo. A word the account forgets comes back past every version it had, so a remove from before can't take a later add, and a cursor from before its removal is refused `410 invalid_cursor`, so the device reads everything again. Adding a word journals its photo again, so a device that dropped the photo gets it back with the word.
photoWord.entityId: The photo's SHA-256, a slash, and the item: `<photo>/<item>`, the item as a note's is.

add.description: It always applies to a photo the account has, an emptied one too, which it brings back. To a deleted or unknown photo it's rejected `unknown_photo`: drop the word on the device, and the photo if no other word holds it. Past 500 words it's `photo_full`: keep the word on the device. Adding a word the photo is on is applied and changes nothing.

remove.description: It applies only at the word's current version, so an add the remover never saw wins, and the remove conflicts. Removing the photo's last word empties the photo, which syncs as its `delete`.

profilePhoto.description: The profile's photo, a file uploaded with `PUT /v1/photos/{photoId}`. The name and username stay the profile's own, so changing one never conflicts with the other.
profilePhoto.entityId: The account's ID, or left out.

set.description: It applies only at the profile photo's current version (0 for none ever set), so two devices that change it conflict, and the second gets the photo as it is now. Setting the photo it has is applied and changes nothing. An app without `photos:read` may set only a file it uploaded itself (else `photo_not_uploaded`). The file it replaces is deleted, unless a Media Library photo is the same file.

remove.description: It applies only at the current version, so a photo set elsewhere since stays, and the remove conflicts. It syncs as a `delete`.

setting.description:
One of the learner's settings, which follow the account rather than the device. A setting the account doesn't hold comes as a `delete`. The settings:

- `readingAids.furigana` (`true` or `false`): Reading Aids: furigana over kanji.
- `readingAids.romaji` (`true` or `false`): Reading Aids: romaji under Japanese.
- `readingAids.wordMeanings` (`true` or `false`): Reading Aids: each word's meaning.
- `readingAids.kanjiMeanings` (`true` or `false`): Reading Aids: each kanji's meaning.
- `readingAids.translations` (`true` or `false`): Reading Aids: translations.
- `readingAids.translationLanguage` (text of at most 35 characters matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$`): Reading Aids: the language translations are in, as a language tag, such as `en`.
- `readingAids.translationSource` (one of `youTube`, `apple`): Reading Aids: where translations come from: YouTube's captions, or Apple's on the device.
- `readingAids.furiganaHiddenOnKnownWords` (`true` or `false`): Reading Aids: no furigana over the words the learner knows.
- `translate.furigana` (`true` or `false`): Translate's own furigana switch.
- `translate.speechSpeed` (a number from 0.5 to 2): How fast Translate speaks: 1 is normal speed.
- `search.sort` (text of at most 120 characters matching `^(default|known-words|frequency\|[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,99})$`): Search results' Sorted by: `default`, `known-words`, or `frequency|` and a frequency dictionary's family.
- `search.filter` (one of `all`, `known`, `unknown`, `learning`): Search results' filter.
- `imageSearch.textView` (one of `photo`, `both`, `text`, `translate`): Image Search's view: the photo, the photo and its text, the text, or its translation.
- `frequencyDictionaries.chosen` (text of at most 5,000 characters matching `^([a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,99}(,[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,99}){0,49})?$`): The frequency dictionaries the learner chose, by pack ID, in their order, separated by commas: at most 50, and empty for none. Each device downloads its own copy.
setting.entityId: The setting's name, from the list above.

set.description: It applies only at the setting's current version (0 for one never set), so two devices that change one setting conflict, and the second gets the value as it is now; settings change apart, so changing one never conflicts with another. Setting the value it has is applied and changes nothing. A name the service doesn't know is rejected `unknown_setting`, and a value out of its kind `invalid_fields`: keep the device's value either way.

recentSearch.description: A search the learner made, as the app's recent searches list it. The account keeps the 50 with the latest `searchedAt`, and remembers the latest 100 it removed or pruned, as it does Player's Recent.
recentSearch.entityId: The HMAC-SHA256 of the query in UTF-8, after Unicode NFC, under the account's `searchKey` from the sync answer, in 64 lowercase hex digits: one query is one entity on every device, and a removed one keeps nothing that shows what was searched without the key. The examples use a key of 64 zeros.

search.description: A search of a query the account has applies whatever its base version, and the later `searchedAt` is kept. A search of a query the learner removed applies only at the removal's version, so one made before seeing the removal conflicts with the `delete`. A search past the 50 newest prunes the oldest, which syncs as a `delete`.

remove.description: The learner removed the search, or cleared them all, one `remove` each. It always applies; removing one the account has not is applied and changes nothing.

x-sync-rejections.invalid_fields: A field is missing, isn't one the operation takes, or is out of bounds.
x-sync-rejections.unknown_entity: The service syncs no such entity, as when it is older than the app. Keep the change, and send the entity again once the service knows it.
x-sync-rejections.unknown_operation: The entity has no such operation.
x-sync-rejections.invalid_mutation: `entityId` isn't in the entity's form, or `baseVersion` is missing from an operation that reads it.
x-sync-rejections.mutation_id_reused: The ID was used for a different mutation. Give each mutation its own.
x-sync-rejections.already_exists: The account has, or had, a list with that ID.
x-sync-rejections.unknown_list: The list word's list isn't in the account, or was deleted.
x-sync-rejections.too_many_notes: The account has 10,000 notes. Keep the note on the device, untouched.
x-sync-rejections.unknown_photo: The photo word's photo isn't in the account, or was deleted: drop the word on the device, and the photo if no other word holds it.
x-sync-rejections.photo_not_uploaded: The account holds no file for that photo: upload it with `PUT /v1/photos/{photoId}`, then send the change again under a new ID.
x-sync-rejections.photo_full: The photo is on 500 words. Keep the word on the device.
x-sync-rejections.unknown_setting: The service syncs no setting of that name, as when it is older than the app. Keep the setting on the device, and send it again once the service knows it.
x-sync-rejections.not_allowed: The app's scopes don't include the operation's.

changes.description: Each entity of the kind, once, as it is now, in the order the account last changed them, oldest first: a `put`, or a `delete` for one removed, as sync answers them.

cursor.description: Opaque, and at most 200 characters. Send it to read the rest, or, later, what changed since.

hasMore.description: More are waiting: read again with the new cursor.

status.description: `none`: The account has never had a subscription. `active`: Paid through `expiresAt`. It renews then unless `willRenew` is false. `grace_period`: A renewal's payment failed, and the store is retrying it. The subscription's features stay on until `expiresAt`. `billing_retry`: A renewal's payment failed, and the store is retrying it. The features are off until it's paid. `pending`: The first payment is still being made. The features are off until it is. `paused`: Paused where it was bought. The features are off until it resumes. `expired`: It ended: canceled, or never paid again. The features are off. `revoked`: Refunded, or revoked by the store. The features are off.

active.description: Whether the subscription's features are on now: `status` is `active`, or `grace_period`, and `expiresAt` hasn't passed.

source.description: Where it was bought: `apple`, in the App Store, or `stripe`, on the website.

productId.description: The App Store product's ID, or the Stripe price's.

expiresAt.description: When the paid time, or the grace period, ends. A subscription set to renew keeps its features for a day past it while the renewal reaches the service.

willRenew.description: Whether it renews at `expiresAt`. `null` until the store has said.

managedIn.description: Where it was bought, so where the learner changes, cancels, or fixes the payment of one still running: `app_store`, in the App Store's subscription settings, or `website`, through POST /v1/me/subscription/portal. A subscription that no longer runs keeps it, to say where it was bought; only `running` is managed. `null` when the account never had one.

running.description: Every subscription still running for the account, in either store, each managed where it was bought. Usually one; two when the learner subscribed in both, which the app and the website show, so each can be managed or canceled where it was bought.

canSubscribe.description: Whether to offer a subscription. False while one runs anywhere, in a grace period, a billing retry, or a pause too, so a learner is never offered a second.

cloudAccess.description: What POST /v1/sync and the photo files' routes do for this app now: `subscribed` and `free` sync, and `subscription_required` refuses with `402 subscription_required`, the app's cue for the paywall.

appAccountToken.description: The account's `appAccountToken`: the app sets it on every App Store purchase, so the purchase belongs to this account. It never changes. The app that sells the subscription always gets one; another app gets null until the account first buys or is answered for that app, so no record is made for an account that never subscribes.

website.description: The Stripe price IDs the website offers. Empty where Stripe is off.

offers.description: What to offer when `canSubscribe` is true.

plans.description: Each of `offers.website`, in its order, as Stripe describes it. Empty where Stripe is off.

The service takes `checkout.session.*`, `customer.subscription.*`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `refund.*`, `charge.dispute.*`, and `radar.early_fraud_warning.created`, reads each subscription's state from Stripe as it is then, and records every charge, refund, dispute, and fraud warning in its ledger.

put.description: The file of a Media Library photo or the profile photo, before the sync change that names it (`photo`'s `add`, or `profilePhoto`'s `set`). The body is the file's bytes, at most 12 MB, JPEG, PNG, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, GIF, WebP, TIFF, or BMP; the service reads the type from the bytes, not from `Content-Type`, and keeps them as they are. Uploading a file the account holds changes nothing, unless its storage lost it, which this puts back. A file no photo names 24 hours after its upload is deleted. An account holds at most 1,000 files, the profile photo's and an emptied photo's for its 30 days included. An app with only `profile` holds at most 2 files it uploaded, the profile photo and the one replacing it, which may be ones the Media Library holds too; it's answered as though the library held nothing, `201` or `409`, so it learns nothing of the library, and may set only a file it uploaded as the profile photo.

post.description: With `idToken`, signs in with the token the device got, and makes the account on the first sign-in. Without it, starts the web sign-in, which comes back to GET /v1/auth/callback/{id}. A new account's email must be verified by the provider, and an email that already has an account is refused until the learner adds this way while signed in.

schema.description: The language of the page the request comes from: `ja` or `en`. The email the request sends is in it, and an account the request makes keeps it for the emails sent later without one. Any other value, or none, means the account's language, or English. `Accept-Language` is never read.
